{{Short description|Theorem in group theory}}
The '''universal embedding theorem''', or '''Krasner–Kaloujnine universal embedding theorem''', is a theorem from the mathematical discipline of [[group theory]] first published in 1951 by [[Marc Krasner]] and [[Lev Kaluznin]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Kaloujnine|Krasner|1951a}}.</ref> The theorem states that any [[group extension]] of a group {{math|''H''}} by a group {{math|''A''}} is isomorphic to a subgroup of the regular [[wreath product]] {{math|''A''&nbsp;Wr&nbsp;''H''.}} The theorem is named for the fact that the group {{math|''A''&nbsp;Wr&nbsp;''H''}} is said to be ''[[Universal property|universal]]'' with respect to all extensions of {{math|''H''}} by {{math|''A''.}}

==Statement==
Let {{math|''H''}} and {{math|''A''}} be groups, let {{math|''K''&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''A''<sup>''H''</sup>}} be the set of all functions from {{math|''H''}} to {{math|''A'',}} and consider the [[Group action (mathematics)|action]] of {{math|''H''}} on itself by multiplication. This action extends naturally to an action of {{math|''H''}} on {{math|''K''}}, defined as <math>(h\cdot \phi)(g)=\phi(h^{-1}g),</math> where <math>\phi\in K,</math> and {{math|''g''}} and {{math|''h''}} are both in {{math|''H''.}} This is an automorphism of {{math|''K'',}} so we can construct the [[semidirect product]] {{math|''K''&nbsp;⋊&nbsp;''H''}}, which is termed the ''regular [[wreath product]]'', and denoted {{math|''A''&nbsp;Wr&nbsp;''H''}} or <math>A\wr H.</math> The group {{math|''K''&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''A''<sup>''H''</sup>}} (which is isomorphic to <math>\{(\phi,1)\in A\wr H:\phi\in K\}</math>) is called the ''base group'' of the wreath product.

The '''Krasner–Kaloujnine universal embedding theorem''' states that if {{math|''G''}} has a [[normal subgroup]] {{math|''A''}} and {{math|''H''&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''G''/''A'',}} then there is an [[Injective function|injective]] [[homomorphism]] of groups <math>\theta:G\to A\wr H</math> such that {{math|''A''}} maps [[Surjective function|surjectively]] onto <math>\text{im}(\theta)\cap K.</math><ref>{{harvtxt|Dixon |Mortimer |1996 |p=47 }}.</ref> This is equivalent to the wreath product {{math|''A''&nbsp;Wr&nbsp;''H''}} having a subgroup isomorphic to {{math|''G'',}} where {{math|''G''}} is any extension of {{math|''H''}} by {{math|''A''.}}

==Proof==
This proof comes from Dixon–Mortimer.<ref name=DM>{{harvtxt |Dixon |Mortimer |1996 |pp=47–48 }}.</ref>

Define a homomorphism <math>\psi:G\to H</math> whose kernel is {{math|''A''.}} Choose a set <math>T=\{t_u:u\in H\}</math> of (right) coset representatives of {{math|''A''}} in {{math|''G'',}} where <math>\psi(t_u)=u.</math> Then for all {{math|''x''}} in {{math|''G'',}} <math>t_u^{-1} x t_{\psi(x)^{-1}u}\in\ker \psi=A.</math> For each {{math|''x''}} in {{math|''G'',}} we define a function <math>f_x:H\to A</math> such that <math>f_x(u)=t_u^{-1} x t_{\psi(x)^{-1}u}.</math> Then the embedding <math>\theta</math> is given by <math>\theta(x)=(f_x,\psi(x))\in A\wr H.</math>

We now prove that this is a homomorphism. If {{math|''x''}} and {{math|''y''}} are in {{math|''G'',}} then <math>\theta(x)\theta(y)=(f_x(\psi(x).f_y),\psi(xy)).</math> Now <math>\psi(x).f_y(u)=f_y(\psi(x)^{-1}u),</math> so for all {{math|''u''}} in {{math|''H'',}}
:<math>f_x(u)(\psi(x).f_y(u)) = t_u^{-1} x t_{\psi(x)^{-1}u} t_{\psi(x)^{-1}u}^{-1} y t_{\psi(y)^{-1}\psi(x)^{-1}u}=t_u xy t^{-1}_{\psi(xy)^{-1}u},</math>
so {{math|''f''<sub>''x''</sub>&nbsp;''f''<sub>''y''</sub>&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''f''<sub>''xy''</sub>.}} Hence <math>\theta</math> is a homomorphism as required. 

The homomorphism is injective. If <math>\theta(x)=\theta(y),</math> then both {{math|''f''<sub>''x''</sub>(''u'')&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''f''<sub>''y''</sub>(''u'')}} (for all ''u'') and <math>\psi(x)=\psi(y).</math> Then <math>t_u^{-1} x t_{\psi(x)^{-1}u}=t_u^{-1} y t_{\psi(y)^{-1}u},</math> but we can cancel <math>t^{-1}_{u}</math> and <math>t_{\psi(x)^{-1}u}=t_{\psi(y)^{-1}u}</math> from both sides, so {{math|''x''&nbsp;{{=}}&nbsp;''y'',}} hence <math>\theta</math> is injective. Finally, <math>\theta(x)\in K</math> precisely when <math>\psi(x)=1,</math> in other words when <math>x\in A</math> (as <math>A=\ker\psi</math>).

==Generalizations and related results==
*The [[Krohn–Rhodes theory#Definitions and description of the Krohn–Rhodes theorem|Krohn–Rhodes theorem]] is a statement similar to the universal embedding theorem, but for [[semigroup]]s. A semigroup {{math|''S''}} is a ''divisor'' of a semigroup {{math|''T''}} if it is the [[image]] of a [[subsemigroup]] of {{math|''T''}} under a homomorphism. The theorem states that every finite semigroup {{math|''S''}} is a divisor of a finite alternating wreath product of finite [[simple group]]s (each of which is a divisor of {{math|''S''}}) and finite [[aperiodic semigroup]]s.
*An alternate version of the theorem exists which requires only a group {{math|''G''}} and a subgroup {{math|''A''}} (not necessarily normal).<ref>{{harvtxt |Kaloujnine |Krasner |1951b}}.</ref> In this case, {{math|''G''}} is isomorphic to a subgroup of the regular wreath product {{math|''A''&nbsp;Wr&nbsp;(''G''/Core(''A'')).}}
